title: Galaxy router: in-process system shards on demand
description: The single application instance hosts any number of system shards in-process: the router spawns a shard when a player joins its system, reaps it when empty (after a grace period), and enforces a per-system occupancy cap.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server/galaxy/router.ts: Router.getShard(systemId) returns the active shard or creates one (load system data from shared generators with GALAXY_SEED, load ships via TASK-24); Router.reapEmpty() stops shards with zero connections after a 60 s grace (ships flushed first)

Cap enforcement: join_system into a shard already at 16 players returns {code:'system-full'} and the player stays in their previous system; cap is the constant MAX_PLAYERS_PER_SYSTEM = 16 in src/shared
Router stats: GET /api/galaxy/health (auth) lists active shards with {systemId, players, uptimeMs} — used by the chart UI occupancy dots (TASK-7)
Concurrent spawn test: 10 clients joining 3 different systems in parallel — all get correct, distinct shard state (no cross-system bleed, asserted by checking per-system unique entity ids)
Reap test: all players leave a shard, after 60 s (fake timers) the shard stops and its ships are flushed (DB rows present with correct positions)
Restart test: join system A, restart the server process, join system A again — same world (positions from DB, AI placement identical given seed)

steps.details: Map<systemId, Shard>; getShard is idempotent and synchronous after load (load is async, use a pending-promise map to collapse concurrent spawns). reapEmpty on a 5 s interval; grace timer per shard; on reap: flushShips, sim.stop(), delete from map.

WS 'join_system' handler: router.getShard → cap check → shard.addConnection(conn) (broadcasts presence, sends initial full snapshot) → on leave: shard.removeConnection, start grace. Player's 'current system' tracked in ConnState.
GET /api/galaxy/health (auth) → {shards: [{systemId, name, players, uptimeMs}]}. Read-only, cheap.
Concurrent-spawn, reap (fake timers), cap, restart tests per acceptance; run full suite + typecheck.

technicalNotes: System data (stars, planets, stations) is derived deterministically from GALAXY_SEED (TASK-3/4/5) — the shard caches it in memory; only ships/players persist (PRD §6).
Shard load time budget: < 500 ms for a typical system (measured in the concurrent-spawn test; surface chunk generation is lazy, not upfront).
This is the v1 single-instance design; the Router interface is the seam a future process-level shard manager would replace.
